quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: CFO Toshiyasu Horie (results briefing Q&A, Q1 fiscal 2026): the full-year forecast was not revised at this time and will be reviewed in detail at the Q2 earnings announcement in November; however, given income growth centered on First Priority businesses, operating income is likely to exceed the previous forecast of JPY 248 billion, and performance is progressing extremely well.
quarterly_data.figure: operating income likely to exceed the previous forecast of JPY 248 billion

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Takuya Takahashi, Material; results briefing Q&A): demand for electronic materials, particularly for AI-related applications, is expected to remain strong and has often exceeded the company's expectations recently; however, shipments of camera module ICs are projected to decline due to lower smartphone production resulting from memory shortages. From Q1 to Q2 the company expects operating income to decline across all Material businesses on the anticipated appreciation of the yen and a seasonal increase in fixed costs.

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Nobuaki Hashimoto, Electronics; results briefing Q&A): Q1 sales of Pimel increased by approximately 30% year on year, while glass fabric and dry film photoresist each grew by approximately 20%; camera module IC sales declined by a single-digit percentage year on year due to lower smartphone sales resulting from memory shortages.
quarterly_data.figure: Pimel approximately +30% YoY; glass fabric approximately +20%; dry film photoresist approximately +20%; camera module ICs down single-digit %

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Nobuaki Hashimoto, Electronics; results briefing Q&A): development of quartz glass fabric and low-CTE (low thermal expansion) glass fabric is progressing smoothly, with no change to the schedule of obtaining customer qualification during FY 2026 and beginning to make a meaningful contribution to sales from FY 2027 onward.
quarterly_data.figure: customer qualification during FY 2026; meaningful sales contribution from FY 2027 onward

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Nobuaki Hashimoto, Electronics; results briefing Q&A) on glass fabric pricing: the high value-added strategy is progressing as planned and the sales mix of next generation glass fabric is gradually expanding; in addition to the mix change, the company expects average selling prices to gradually improve reflecting higher raw material costs.

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Nobuya Kaneko, Energy & Infrastructure; results briefing Q&A): Q1 sales volume of Hipore wet-process LIB separators for ESS applications increased more than tenfold year on year, driven primarily by grid-connected energy storage systems, a market the company began serving in Q4 of FY 2025; that demand is rising on electricity demand from the expansion of generative AI and data centers and on renewable adoption, and the company expects it to remain strong from Q2 onward. Sales for BBUs (battery backup units) protecting data centers from momentary power interruptions are also increasing and expected to keep growing steadily. The company is exploring expanding sales of coated separators for ESS applications to improve profitability.
quarterly_data.figure: ESS separator sales volume more than tenfold YoY in Q1

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Nobuya Kaneko, Energy & Infrastructure; results briefing Q&A): the Q1 year-on-year operating income decline was attributable to separators, with the divestiture of the lead battery separator business a main factor; profit growth from higher ESS volumes was limited by the mix shift toward ESS applications (different profitability from consumer electronics and automotive) and higher fixed costs from increased capacity utilization. For the full year the company expects separator volumes to rise for ESS and automotive applications, operating income to remain at roughly the previous year's level and EBITDA to improve. Automotive sales have recently been somewhat soft due to the timing and status of the programs adopting its products, and because the separator business primarily targets North America it has not benefited significantly from the European EV demand recovery.

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Takuya Takahashi, Material; results briefing Q&A): inventory valuation, including inventory variance, had a positive impact of slightly more than JPY 20 billion in Q1 versus the same period last year, approximately 90% attributable to Essential Chemical; the company expects a negative impact of approximately JPY 10 billion year on year in Q2 and a positive impact in the low JPY 10 billion range for H1, narrowing further for the full year as naphtha prices are expected to decline further in H2. A temporary demand increase was seen in Comfort Life consumables in April and May (not significant for Material as a whole), and no significant demand decline from rising raw material prices has been seen.
quarterly_data.figure: Q1 inventory valuation impact slightly more than +JPY 20 billion YoY (about 90% Essential Chemical); Q2 approximately -JPY 10 billion YoY expected; H1 low JPY 10 billion range positive

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Seiji Nakano, Healthcare; results briefing Q&A): of the JPY 14.4 billion year-on-year Q1 sales increase in Pharmaceuticals & Life Science, JPY 11.5 billion came from Pharmaceuticals (higher shipments of Envarsus XR and Tarpeyo, higher Tarpeyo royalty income - its China and Europe sales rights are licensed out to partners, with royalties up on strong sales particularly in China - and royalty income from Prevymis following consolidation of Aicuris Anti-infective Cures AG) and JPY 2.9 billion from Life Science (higher Planova virus removal filter shipments and the weak yen).
quarterly_data.figure: Pharmaceuticals & Life Science Q1 sales +JPY 14.4 billion YoY (Pharmaceuticals JPY 11.5 billion; Life Science JPY 2.9 billion)

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Seiji Nakano, Healthcare; results briefing Q&A) on Tarpeyo: excluding revenue shifted from Q4 2024 into Q1 2025, underlying Q1 sales growth was approximately 20% year on year, largely in line with expectations. The FY 2026 outlook was lowered from 20-30% growth (U.S. dollar basis) to high teens to around 20%, mainly due to a temporary shortage of U.S. sales representatives (nephrology turnover and sales-organization changes) that slowed new patient prescriptions in Q1; hiring is largely complete and new prescriptions are expected to recover from Q2. The company will continue efforts to achieve approximately 20% growth in FY 2026, is accelerating the integration of the commercial organizations of Veloxis Pharmaceuticals and Calliditas Therapeutics, sees the impact of competing drugs as limited, and still views Tarpeyo as able to reach its peak sales potential of $500 million sooner than originally anticipated at the acquisition.
quarterly_data.figure: Tarpeyo FY 2026 growth outlook high teens to around 20% (previously 20-30%); peak sales potential $500 million

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Seiji Nakano, Healthcare; results briefing Q&A): Envarsus XR sales growth in H1 of FY 2026 is expected in the high teens year on year (U.S. dollar basis), with the full-year outlook unchanged and the FY 2020-FY 2026 CAGR expected to remain in the 20% range. Royalty income from Prevymis, licensed to Merck & Co., is tracking above previous-forecast assumptions; discussions with the U.S. FDA on pritelivir are progressing smoothly, with launch still expected around Q3 of FY 2026 and slightly less than JPY 1 billion of sales expected in H2 of FY 2026 (depending on exchange rates); the negative impact of the Aicuris consolidation on full-year results is expected to be smaller than previously forecast, although R&D expenses will rise as development of AIC468 progresses.
quarterly_data.figure: Envarsus XR H1 growth high teens; pritelivir launch around Q3 FY 2026, slightly less than JPY 1 billion H2 sales

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Seiji Nakano, Healthcare; results briefing Q&A): in Critical Care, ACT sales rose 11% year on year in Q1 (U.S. dollar basis), driven primarily by professional-use defibrillators led by Zenix, with solid momentum expected from Q2; CMS sales including LifeVest rose 11%, with volume up in the U.S. and internationally (particularly strong growth in Germany, France and Italy) and revenue per patient growing steadily.
quarterly_data.figure: ACT sales +11% YoY; CMS (incl. LifeVest) sales +11% YoY (U.S. dollar basis)

quarterly_data.quarter: Asahi Kasei results briefing Q&A: Q&A at Financial Results Briefing for Q1 Fiscal 2026 (07-31-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management (Kensuke Sakai, Homes; results briefing Q&A): Q1 domestic order-built home orders were strong on more large-scale projects, particularly multi-dwelling homes, helped by the corporate-referral sales team set up in FY 2025; the company is monitoring cost increases linked to the Middle East situation. The Overseas Homes Q1 operating loss was primarily attributable to the North American business (lower housing demand, lower volume of work and pricing), while the Australian business remained profitable; management does not perceive a high risk of impairment in North America at this time.
